Zverev holds off Shelton to win US Open title
item.description:
Alexander Zverev held off Ben Shelton to win the US Open on Sunday, capturing the second Grand Slam of his career just months after winning the French Open.
The top-seeded German ruthlessly snuffed out a late surge by Shelton to triumph 6-3, 7-6 (7/2), 5-7, 6-2, crushing the eighth seed's hopes of becoming the first US man in 23 years to win a Grand Slam title.
Zverev expunged the bitter memory of his 2020 US Open defeat, when he was two points from victory before falling to Dominic Thiem in five sets.
It would be six years -- with two major finals disappointments -- before he would break through this season.
"I think God has seen how hard we worked, how much we suffered, how much pain we went through and I think 2026 is the outcome of all the years that happened before," Zverev said at the trophy presentation.
The 23-year-old Shelton was one month shy of his first birthday when Andy Roddick hoisted the 2003 US Open trophy in the last major triumph for a US man.
Hopes were high that Shelton could end the drought after his epic five-set quarter-final victory over defending champion Carlos Alcaraz, and a come-from-behind win over compatriot Frances Tiafoe in the semi-finals.
But Zverev's all-court excellence proved too much for Shelton, despite the support of a star-studded Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd trying to will the American to victory.
With their backing, Shelton surged in the third set, eliminating the errors that Zverev had ruthlessly exploited.
Serving to extend the set, Zverev fell behind 0-40. Shelton fired long on his first set point but on the second Zverev's forehand volley went wide. Shelton had his first break of the match and they were headed to a fourth set.
Zverev, however, responded immediately and decisively, breaking Shelton in the first game of the fourth set and rolling home.
He lifted his arms in triumph after Shelton fired a serve return long on match point and finally received his own huge cheer from the crowd -- but not before some prompting.
Zverev said he didn't initially realize he'd won because he had lost track of the score.
"I knew I broke him twice, but I thought it was 5-1 instead of 6-2, which helped me in a way, because I didn't really get nervous serving out the match," Zverev said.
"In that moment I was in the zone a lot. I didn't hear noise at all. Then also, of course, when the crowd is loud, it's impossible to hear the umpire, so I didn't hear that she said, 'Game, set, match.'"
Zverev had followed up his French Open victory with a runner-up finish at Wimbledon.
But his New York prospects had looked bleak as he labored through two five-setters to start the tournament.
Now the 29-year-old ranked second in the world has a chance to challenge for the number one ranking with Italian Jannik Sinner currently sidelined by a knee injury.
With this win, Zverev said he might consider himself the best player in the world "right, right now."
"If everyone is healthy, I think Jannik is still ahead."

item.description:
Bangladesh suffered a heavy 10-0 defeat to North Korea in their opening match of the Asian Games women’s football tournament on Monday, with the formidable North Korean side scoring seven times in the first half.
Bangladesh struggled to cope with North Korea’s pace and attacking pressure as the East Asian side raced into a commanding lead before the break.

The North Koreans, who have enjoyed considerable success at youth level, are among the favourites for the women’s football gold medal in Japan.
Striker Ri Song A, who was born and raised in Japan, was in North Korea’s starting line-up and also found the net in the second half.
Several hundred pro-Pyongyang supporters, many dressed in red, created a lively atmosphere in Osaka as they sang and chanted throughout the match.
The North Korean teams were welcomed by supporters waving flags when they arrived for the Games last week, wearing white blazers and pink ties.
More than 100 North Korean athletes are competing in 14 sports at the Games, which are being held in Nagoya-Aichi and officially open on September 19.
North Korea suspended participation in international sporting competitions during the pandemic but returned to the Asian Games at Hangzhou in 2023 and also competed at the Paris Olympics.
North Korea's women's team will next face South Korea in a Group F clash on September 21.
The North Korean men's team will begin their campaign against China on Wednesday.

item.title: Dhaka air 6th worst in world Monday morning
item.description:
The air quality in Dhaka turned 'unhealthy' on Monday morning, compared with Sunday's 'unhealthy for sensitive groups' level.
Dhaka ranked 6th on the list of cities with the worst air quality in the world this morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 160 at 8:35am.
The air quality was classified as ‘unhealthy’, meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Singapore topped the list with an AQI score of 169, followed by Malaysia’s Kuala Lumpur with 167 and Indonesia’s Jakarta with 165.
Earlier on Sunday morning, Dhaka ranked 11th among the world’s cities with the worst air quality, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 108 at 9:15 am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as “unhealthy for sensitive groups”, posing health risks to children, older adults, and people with heart or lung diseases, while the general public is mostly unaffected.
An AQI reading of 101 to 150 is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, while 151 to 200 is classified as ‘unhealthy’. A reading between 201 and 300 is considered ‘very unhealthy’, and anything above 301 is categorized as ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides a daily indication of air quality by measuring the level of pollution and its potential impact on human health.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants—particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and ozone.
Dhaka has long faced serious air pollution problems, with air quality generally deteriorating during the winter months and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution contributes to around 7 million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer, and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Harun’s family receives PM’s gift 12 years after his death
item.description:
More than 12 years after Jubo Dal leader Mohammad Harunur Rashid was killed in police firing in Feni, his family has finally received a new home.
BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi handed over the keys to the newly built house to Harunur’s family at Jagatjibanpur in Farhadnagar Union of the district on Sunday. His wife, Bibi Zohra, daughter Majeda Akter and son Touhidul Islam received the keys.
According to district BNP sources, Harunur was killed in police firing on December 4, 2013, amid tensions surrounding a BNP-led programme in support of a hartal on Shaheed Shahidullah Kaiser Road in Feni town. He was then vice-president of the Farhadnagar Union Jubo Dal.
After his death, his wife and children endured years of hardship, including uncertainty over their livelihood and housing.
The new house was built in Jagatjibanpur under an initiative of “Amra BNP Poribar” to rehabilitate the family, following instructions from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. Construction began on April 12.
Speaking at the key handover ceremony, Ruhul Kabir Rizvi accused the previous Awami League government of enforced disappearances and killings.
“Sheikh Hasina did not hesitate to kill anyone to consolidate power. Enforced disappearances and killings continued for 17 years,” he said.
Local BNP leaders recalled Harunur’s political contributions and pledged to continue supporting his family.
The family expressed relief after finally receiving a secure home following years of housing difficulties, though the loss of their husband and father continues to leave a deep void in their lives.
After the ceremony, Rizvi visited Harunur’s grave and inaugurated the nameplate of the new house.

item.title: Chevron team meets PM, discusses investment in Bangladesh’s gas sector
item.description:
A high-level delegation from Chevron met Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday and discussed the US energy giant’s potential investment in Bangladesh’s energy sector, particularly gas.
President of Chevron’s Base Assets and Emerging Countries Javier La Rosa led the delegation during the meeting held at the Prime Minister’s Office at Bangladesh Secretariat in the morning, said a release issued by the PM’s press wing.
During the meeting, the delegation discussed increasing Chevron’s investment in Bangladesh’s existing and mature gas fields, as well as exploring opportunities for investment in new gas fields.
The discussions came amid the government’s efforts to strengthen domestic gas production and attract investment to the energy sector to meet the country’s growing energy demand.
Prime Minister’s Adviser on Finance and Planning Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit, Chevron Bangladesh President and Managing Director Shu Xiong and senior officials concerned were present.

item.title: Bangladesh, Pakistan agree to further strengthen bilateral ties
item.description:
Pakistan High Commissioner to Bangladesh Imran Haider on Sunday paid a courtesy call on President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, with discussions focusing on the positive momentum in bilateral relations and multifaceted cooperation between the two countries.
The president welcomed the high commissioner and thanked Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari for his felicitation message on his assumption of office.
In response to an invitation from the Pakistani president to visit Pakistan, President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said he would like to undertake the visit at the earliest convenience.
Recalling the shared history, common faith, and cultural and familial ties between the peoples of Pakistan and Bangladesh, the president said these associations provide a strong foundation for enhancing mutually beneficial bilateral cooperation across a wide range of sectors.
He expressed satisfaction over the upward trajectory of cooperation in areas including healthcare, science and technology, culture and people-to-people exchanges.
The two sides also discussed cooperation in pharmaceuticals, ceramics and agriculture.
The high commissioner thanked the president for receiving him and briefed him on various ongoing initiatives.
He said medical tourism from Bangladesh to Pakistan was increasing and Pakistani health professionals were training their Bangladeshi counterparts in organ transplantation to develop domestic capacity and reduce treatment costs for Bangladeshi patients.
Under the Pakistan-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor, around 200 Bangladeshi students have enrolled in top-ranking Pakistani universities, while training courses are also being organised for Bangladeshi civil servants.
On direct air connectivity, Haider highlighted the growing demand for increased flight frequencies and the opening of additional routes.
The president observed that enhanced connectivity was crucial to increasing business, cultural and people-to-people contacts.
Haider said there was huge untapped potential for bilateral cooperation that could be realised through concerted efforts by both sides.
He reaffirmed the commitment of the Pakistani leadership to expanding cooperation with Bangladesh across all areas of mutual interest.
The two sides agreed to build on the existing momentum and further strengthen bilateral ties through closer and sustained engagement.

item.title: Gopalganj university library struggles with books, space, technology
item.description:
A shortage of academic and reference books, inadequate seating, slow internet and a lack of modern technological facilities are hampering study and research at the central library of Gopalganj Science and Technology University (GSTU).
The library, established in 2014, has 36,152 books, including academic publications, Liberation War-related books, fiction and novels. It also has around 1,500 printed journals and 500 magazines.
Despite the collection, students say the library lacks many course-specific and specialised books needed for their studies. It also does not have adequate access to international journals, e-books or modern digital facilities. An anti-plagiarism software system for teachers has yet to be introduced, while students do not have computers for academic use.
As a result, students say the library is yet to become an effective centre for higher education, research and knowledge practice.
A visit to the library found several air conditioners and fans out of order. There are also not enough desks for students, while chairs are placed so close together that users have to move them to get in and out. The movement creates noise that can be heard across the reading room, disrupting study.
Students have demanded high-speed internet, books according to their academic needs, a job corner and modernisation of the library.
Alamgir Hossain, a student of the 2018-19 academic session in the Department of Bangla, said around 9,320 students are currently studying at the university, while the library has seating capacity for only about 200.
“The student-to-seat ratio is around 1:50. There are not enough seats. Besides, the internet is slow and there is a shortage of necessary books. Noise from the surrounding areas also disrupts our studies,” he said.
Tamin Iqbal, a student of the 2019-20 academic session, said the library should serve as a centre for higher education, research and knowledge practice, but the existing facilities prevent it from playing that role.
“The number of students has increased, but the number of seats has not. The seating capacity must be increased. We also need high-speed internet. We hope the authorities will resolve these problems quickly,” he said.
Yaminur Rahman Arik, a student of the 2021-22 academic session, said the library lacked adequate subject-specific and reference books.
“Students come here to find books that are unavailable in the hall libraries, but often we cannot find them. There are also not enough reference books. The library does not provide enough scope for developing our knowledge and intellect through study,” he said.
“As a result, many students are frustrated and have become reluctant to use the library. We hope it will be turned into a proper centre for higher education, research and knowledge practice,” he added.
Acting Librarian Nasirul Islam said the library building has two floors, although it was originally planned as a four-storey facility.
“We are facing problems because of space and staff shortages. There is no automation system either, so we have to perform our work manually,” he said.
The library remains open from 9am to 10pm every day, he said, adding that staff members have to work in 13 shifts a week, putting additional pressure on them.
“Despite this, we are trying to provide the best possible services to students. The new vice-chancellor has discussed modernising and expanding the library with us and has assured us that he will work to resolve its problems,” Nasirul said.
Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Md Sohel Hasan, who was appointed on August 25, said he was aware of the problems facing the library.
“I have heard about the problems of the library. We will take initiatives to make it more up-to-date by adding reference books on various subjects, international research journals and reliable sources of information beyond textbooks,” he said.
“We want to create a library that will help teachers and students contribute more effectively to education and research. It will also be developed in a way that helps students prepare for competitive examinations, including the BCS,” the vice-chancellor added.

item.title: Boat race draws thousands to Titas River after two-year hiatus
item.description:
Thousands of spectators lined both banks of the Titas River in Brahmanbaria on Sunday as a colourful traditional boat race returned after a two-year hiatus.
Organised by the district administration, the race began at around 3:30pm along the stretch between Shimrailkandi and Medda areas of the district town.
Nine boats from different parts of Brahmanbaria took part in the competition, with the boat of Shapla Boys Club from Khamtapur village in Sadar upazila emerging as the winner.
Spectators began gathering along the riverbanks before noon, with the crowd swelling as the race drew closer. Once the competition began, cheers and chants from the packed riverbanks created a festive atmosphere.
The brightly decorated boats raced through the Titas as rowers paddled in unison, drawing loud cheers from supporters.
The last boat race on the Titas was held in 2023. The event is considered an important part of Brahmanbaria’s cultural heritage and traditionally attracts visitors from neighbouring districts.
Roni Alam, an expatriate living in Italy, travelled from Dhaka to watch the race.
“Boat racing is a festival close to our hearts. I came from Dhaka this morning despite the difficulties just to watch it. Seeing the enthusiasm of people on both banks has erased all my fatigue,” he said.
Another spectator, Al Amin Shaheen, said the event had created a festive atmosphere across the district.
“We want the boat race to be organised every year,” he said.
Brahmanbaria Deputy Commissioner Md Abusaid said the boat race was a popular traditional event.
“Boat racing is a festival close to the hearts of the people here. From next year, we will organise it on an even larger scale,” he said.
Brahmanbaria-3 MP Khaled Hossain Mahbub said the event highlighted the district’s cultural heritage amid what he described as recent negative campaigns about Brahmanbaria and its culture on social media.
“This boat race has shown that Brahmanbaria is a cultural capital. Boat racing is an integral part of our heritage,” he said, adding that he hoped the event would be organised regularly from next year.
Prizes were later handed over to the winning team at a ceremony attended by District Council Administrator Sirajul Islam, Deputy Director of the Local Government Division Shariful Islam, Superintendent of Police Shah Md Abdur Rouf, Additional Deputy Commissioner Ranjan Chandra Dey and other officials and local political leaders.

item.title: Fertiliser crunch fuels anger among Bhurungamari farmers
item.description:
Growing demand for fertiliser during the peak Aman season and ahead of early winter vegetable cultivation is fuelling frustration among farmers in Bhurungamari upazila of Kurigram, with many saying they are struggling to obtain supplies from authorised dealers.
The growing discontent has already spilled into protests, road blockades and incidents involving fertiliser dealers, reflecting mounting tensions over distribution.
Farmers also complain that they receive little field-level advice from agriculture officials on which fertiliser or pesticide to use, and in what quantities.
Agriculture officials, however, say there is no overall shortage of fertiliser in the upazila. They blame excessive use and stockpiling by some farmers for putting additional pressure on supplies.
A visit to several unions on Thursday found farmers moving from one sales outlet to another in search of fertiliser. Many said they either failed to get supplies or received much less than they needed.
At 9am, farmers were seen waiting at the BCIC dealer outlet of Messrs Janarddan Chandra Saha at Camp Mor in Bangasonahat Union. Three to five farmers were reportedly sharing one sack of DAP, while urea distribution had been suspended because of insufficient stock.
The farmers said their Aman paddy was around one-and-a-half to nearly two months old and they wanted to apply fertiliser to the fields. Agriculture officials, however, said DAP was not needed at this stage and applying it would be wasteful.
Mohammad Ali and Abdul Aziz, who had collected DAP, said they were unaware that the fertiliser was not recommended for Aman paddy at this stage.
“We do not know which fertiliser should be applied and when. We look at the condition of the plants and apply fertiliser accordingly,” Mohammad Ali said.
Abdul Aziz, who has two bighas of Aman, said he could not obtain urea and was therefore planning to use DAP instead.
“I do not know what else to do. I am using DAP because I could not get urea,” he said.
Abul Hashem, a representative of the dealer, said demand had increased sharply as farmers had begun cultivating eggplant on hundreds of bighas of land in the char areas.
“The demand for fertiliser is very high, but we are not getting enough to meet it,” he said.
In Gunaiyer Kuti char along the Dudhkumar River, farmers were cultivating early-season eggplant on hundreds of bighas of land.
Several farmers said they needed urea and DAP but could not obtain enough. They also complained that block supervisors, or BSs, rarely visit their fields to provide advice.
Instead, representatives of private agrochemical companies often visit the area, and farmers rely on their recommendations, they said.
Hridoy Molla, who has cultivated eggplant on four bighas, said he was unable to obtain fertiliser according to his requirements.
“I am mixing organic fertiliser and magnesium and applying them to the fields. The BSs do not come here. We apply fertiliser based on the condition of the plants,” he said.
Another farmer, Ramadan Ali, said he was also forced to rely on his own experience.
“We do not get fertiliser or advice. No BS comes here. We use our own knowledge to decide what fertiliser and pesticides to apply,” he said.
Kurigram Department of Agricultural Extension Deputy Director Abdullah Al Mamun denied that agriculture officials were disconnected from farmers, but acknowledged that staff shortages made it difficult to reach everyone.
“There is a tendency among farmers in Bhurungamari to apply excessive amounts of fertiliser. Many are seeking fertiliser even when it is not necessary and do not follow the recommended doses,” he said.
“There is no need to apply DAP to Aman paddy at this stage. Doing so would be a waste. After September 20, there will also be no need to apply urea. Many farmers use DAP instead of urea,” he added.
Regarding the farmers’ complaints about a lack of field-level advice, Mamun said BSs were required to visit fields and provide technical support through field days and other programmes.
“There are many farmers in each union, while we have a shortage of manpower. So it may not always be possible to reach everyone. However, BSs are stationed at every union parishad, and farmers can go there for advice whenever necessary,” he said.
Considering the increased demand, the agriculture department has sought an additional allocation of 300 tonnes each of urea and DAP for Bhurungamari, beyond the upazila’s regular allocation, Mamun said.

item.title: IGP: Police must enhance skills, capacity to combat cybercrime
item.description:
Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir on Sunday said there is no alternative to enhancing the skills and capacity of police personnel to combat cybercrime.
He made the remarks while inaugurating a 10-day Training of Trainers (ToT) course on investigation of cybercrime cases at the Police Staff College Bangladesh in Mirpur in Dhaka on Sunday.
“Artificial intelligence, deepfakes, encrypted communication systems and cloud computing have opened new avenues of opportunities, but at the same time created new challenges for law enforcement agencies,” the IGP said.
He said criminals are abusing technology to commit cyber-based fraud, online financial crimes, data theft, hacking, online harassment and digital extortion.
“Changes in the nature of policing have become a demand of the time to tackle the growing cybercrime. Developing investigation capacity to combat cybercrime is extremely essential for modern policing,” he said.
Addressing the police officers attending the training, the IGP said the course would help them acquire not only technical skills but also training and communication skills.
“The knowledge and skills gained through the training must be disseminated among other investigators,” he said, adding that effective training of other investigators would multiply the number of cybercrime case investigators.
The IGP thanked the Training Wing of Police Headquarters and the Police Staff College Bangladesh for arranging the timely training and stressed the need for regularly organising such training and updating training materials and modules.
Police Staff College Bangladesh Rector and Additional IGP Kazi Md Fazlul Karim presided over the programme, while CID chief and Additional IGP Barrister Mohammad Mosharraf Hossain attended as a special guest.
DIG (Training) Md Ekramul Habib delivered the welcome address, while Additional DIG (Training-2) Dr Mosammat Shehela Parveen presented the roadmap and implementation strategy for cybercrime investigation training.
Faculty members and resource persons of Police Staff College Bangladesh were also present.
The Police Staff College Bangladesh organised the 10-day course at the initiative of the Training Branch of Police Headquarters.
A total of 332 police officers participating in the ToT course will, in phases, provide training to field-level investigators of cybercrime cases.

item.title: ASK condemns alleged rape of two dancers hired for wedding event
item.description:
Two women dancers were allegedly gang-raped on the Titas River in Sarail, Brahmanbaria, after being hired to perform at a wedding, Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK) said.
In a statement on Sunday, the rights group condemned the incident and expressed deep concern and outrage.
ASK said the two women were taken aboard a boat on September 11 on the pretext of performing at an event. They were allegedly held hostage at gunpoint and raped for an extended period.
The incident is a grave violation of the women’s safety and dignity and a serious assault on their professional rights and freedom to work, ASK said.
A woman has the fundamental right to pursue her chosen profession with dignity and work in a safe environment, it said. Working as a dancer or performing at an event for payment must not expose anyone to violence or abuse, ASK added.
The organisation said every citizen has the right to work safely, and ensuring such safety is the state’s responsibility.
ASK said the incident should not be viewed merely as a brutal crime committed by a few individuals. It also raises serious questions about the effectiveness of state mechanisms to prevent violence against women, law enforcement, and ensuring women’s safety while travelling and working. ASK demanded the immediate arrest of all those involved and their prosecution following an impartial and professional investigation. It also called for ensuring that no perpetrator escapes justice due to influence or pressure.
The organisation also demanded security, necessary medical treatment, psychological and legal support for the victims, as well as protection of their identities and privacy.
“Women’s safety is not merely a law-and-order issue; it is a question of equal rights, dignity and human rights,” ASK said, stressing that the state must ensure an environment where women can pursue their chosen professions without fear or insecurity.

Salahuddin, IRI delegation discuss cybercrime, online bullying
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Sunday held a meeting with a delegation of the International Republican Institute (IRI), with discussions focusing on preventing cybercrime and online bullying, and the proposed Cyber Security (Amendment) Act 2026.
The courtesy meeting took place at the minister's office at noon.
The delegation was led by IRI Resident Program Director John Fluharty. Helen Jerin Khan, MP, IRI Technical Adviser Ruksana Haque, and young politicians and IRI trainees Chamon Faria and Mohammad Prince were also present.
During the meeting, Fluharty briefed the minister on IRI's ongoing programs aimed at developing youth leadership and promoting violence-free political practices.
He said young people and political activists in Bangladesh are currently facing harassment and defamation due to cyberbullying and organized disinformation.
Fluharty called for a consensus-based policy and legal protection for both the government and opposition parties in this regard.
The minister assured the delegation that the government is aware of citizens' freedom of expression and personal security.
“Under Article 39 of the Constitution, every citizen has the right to express opinions and engage in constructive criticism, subject to reasonable restrictions. However, constructive criticism is not the same as character assassination or abusive language for political purposes,” he said.
Salahuddin said the government has been seeking opinions from the international community, media personalities, senior editors and civil society stakeholders for the past two months as part of efforts to revise the proposed Cyber Security (Amendment) Act.
He said the main objectives of the law is to restore civility in the digital space, protect women and young people from cyberbullying and ensure professional protection for journalists while preventing any misuse of the law.
The minister said the government will welcome constructive recommendations from both international and local stakeholders to strengthen digital security and establish a violence-free political environment.
Additional Home Secretary (Political and Immigration Wings) Dr Ziauddin Ahmed and Joint Secretary of the Political-1 Branch Rebeka Khan, among others, attended the meeting.

item.title: HC: Strikes, hartals against court verdicts illegal
item.description:
The High Court has declared hartals, strikes or work stoppages called in protest against court verdicts or orders illegal and unconstitutional. It also directed the authorities concerned to take legal and criminal action against bus owners’ associations and workers’ organisations if they call transport strikes or hartals in protest against court verdicts or orders.
A High Court bench comprising Justice Shashanka Kumar Sarkar and Justice Faisal Hasan Arif delivered the judgment on Sunday. In its observation, the court said all executive and judicial authorities are bound to comply with Supreme Court verdicts and orders under Article 112 of the Constitution.
An aggrieved party may appeal against a verdict or seek other lawful remedies, the court said, adding that calling a hartal, strike or work stoppage against a court verdict or order is not lawful.
Such programmes not only show disrespect to the judiciary but also run counter to the Constitution, it observed.
The court directed the secretary of the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA), the Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) and other relevant authorities to take necessary legal action if any hartal or strike is called against a court verdict or order.
In August 2011, five people, including filmmaker Tareque Masud and journalist and broadcaster Munier Mishuk, were killed when a Deluxe Paribahan bus collided with a microbus in Ghior upazila of Manikganj.
Following the trial, a Manikganj court sentenced the bus driver on February 22, 2017.
Protesting the sentence, bus owners called a transport strike and hartal. After reports of the programmes appeared in the media, Human Rights and Peace for Bangladesh (HRPB) filed a writ petition with the High Court in the public interest.
On March 1, 2017, a High Court division bench issued a rule and ordered the strike and hartal to be withdrawn within 24 hours and normal traffic movement to be restored. The transport strike was withdrawn the following day.
The final hearing of the rule was later held by the bench of Justice Shashanka Kumar Sarkar and Justice Faisal Hasan Arif. After lengthy proceedings, the court made the rule absolute and delivered the judgment.
During the hearing, senior lawyer Manzil Morshed, appearing for HRPB, told the court that under Article 112 of the Constitution, all concerned authorities are bound to comply with court verdicts and directions.
He said bus owners had shown disrespect to the court by calling a transport strike after the bus driver was convicted in the accident case.

item.title: Chief prosecutor: Threats to witnesses cannot obstruct tribunal proceedings
item.description:
International Crimes Tribunal Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam has said no one will be allowed to threaten or intimidate witnesses in crimes against humanity cases or obstruct judicial proceedings.
He made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists at his office on Sunday afternoon.
Asked about allegations that witnesses were being threatened by the accused in a crimes against humanity case over incidents in Chittagong, Aminul said he had received complaints in this regard.
He said law enforcement agencies had been instructed to take necessary measures to ensure the witnesses’ security.
“If there is evidence that anyone is threatening a witness in a case, legal action can be taken,” he said.
He, however, said threats and intimidation would not be allowed to disrupt the judicial process.
“No investigation or trial before this tribunal can be obstructed through intimidation or threats,” the chief prosecutor said. On a complaint filed by the family seeking justice for the murder of journalist couple Sagar Sarwar and Meherun Runi, Aminul said the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) was currently investigating the case.
He said Megh’s maternal uncle Roman had submitted a written application to the tribunal seeking its intervention.
“Their expectation is that we will also investigate the case or assist the PBI if we receive any information,” he said, adding that the application would be reviewed.
“If the matter does not fall under a widespread or systematic offence, we will inform them accordingly,” Aminul said.
He said anyone had the right to submit an application to the tribunal and that the family had exercised that right.
“The PBI investigation is ongoing. At this point, we consider the Sagar-Runi incident an individual murder case. We will examine whether it falls within the scope of a widespread or systematic offence,” he said.
He added that the application had been accepted, although it was not a matter of formally registering a case at this stage.

item.title: National committee on Chittagong Hill Tracts reconstituted with PM as chairperson
item.description:
The government has reconstituted the National Committee on Chittagong Hill Tracts to set priorities on key issues concerning the region, oversee the implementation of various activities and coordinate security and law-and-order matters.
The prime minister has been appointed chairperson of the 19-member committee, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division on Thursday.
The committee includes nine ministers and advisers, along with the Cabinet secretary, principal secretary to the prime minister, members of parliament elected from the three Hill Tracts districts, the principal coordinator for SDG affairs at the Prime Minister’s Office, and the director generals of National Security Intelligence (NSI) and the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI).
The chief coordinator of the Armed Forces Division under the Ministry of Defence has been appointed chief coordinator of the committee, while the DG of DGFI will serve as the member-secretary.
The committee will set priorities on important issues concerning the Chittagong Hill Tracts and oversee the expenditure and implementation of related activities.
It will also determine the scope of work and operational areas of security forces, law enforcement agencies and other relevant bodies deployed in the region.
Formulating a national strategy for the overall development of the Chittagong Hill Tracts and taking necessary steps to implement it will also be among the committee’s key responsibilities.
According to the notification, the committee may invite relevant officials from any ministry, security force or law enforcement agency to its meetings when necessary.
The Armed Forces Division of the Prime Minister’s Office will perform the institutional and administrative functions of the committee, including secretariat duties.
Md Humayun Kabir, additional secretary of the Cabinet Division, signed the notification by order of the president.

item.title: Four killed in accident while returning from wedding in Chittagong
item.description:
Four people were killed and eight others injured in a head-on collision between a covered van and a microbus in Karnaphuli, Chittagong, while they were returning home after attending a wedding ceremony.
Two of the deceased died at the scene, while the other two succumbed to their injuries after being taken to hospital, police said.
The accident occurred around 2am on Sunday in the College Bazar area of Karnaphuli on the Chittagong-Cox’s Bazar Highway.
According to witnesses, the covered van had crossed the Shah Amanat Bridge and was making a high-speed U-turn in the College Bazar area when it collided with the microbus coming from the opposite direction.
The deceased were identified as Niaz Morshed, 22, his younger sister Mimtah, 17, their maternal uncle Md Ferdous Alam, 55, and microbus driver Md Munna. All of them were residents of Eidgah area in Cox’s Bazar.
Seven of the injured were admitted to Chittagong Medical College Hospital.
Police and eyewitnesses said Mimtah’s elder sister’s wedding was held at a community centre in Agrabad, Chittagong city, on Saturday night. After the ceremony, several family members and relatives were returning to Eidgah in Cox’s Bazar in the microbus when the accident occurred.
Nur Ahmad, officer-in-charge of Karnaphuli police station, told Bangla Tribune that four people died in the accident—two at the scene and two after being taken to hospital.
“The covered van has been seized following the accident, but its driver and assistant fled the scene. Legal action is being taken,” he said.
SI Nurul Alam Ashik of the Chittagong Medical College Hospital police outpost said the accident occurred around 2am in the College Bazar area under Karnaphuli police station.
He said the injured were taken to the hospital.

item.title: Prominent Urdu poet Syed Taqi Mohammad dies
item.description:
Syed Taqi Mohammad, also known as Buddan Saheb, a distinguished Urdu poet and prominent social worker and organiser from Old Dhaka, has died at the age of 76.
He died around 8pm Friday at his residence in the Sat Rawza area of Old Dhaka.
Journalist Tarun Sarkar confirmed the news to the media on Saturday in a press release issued on behalf of the Committee for Commissioning Books on Architecture (Dhakar Sthapotto Bishoyok Grontho Pronoyon Committee).
Syed Taqi Mohammad is survived by his wife and five children.
His namaz-e-janaza was held on Saturday afternoon after Zuhr prayers at Hussaini Dalan Imambara. He was later buried at the family graveyard in Sat Rawza.
Born on January 14, 1950, Syed Taqi Mohammad belonged to an aristocratic Mughal family in Sat Rawza. His father, Nawab Syed Ali Mohammad, known as Chhotton, was a prominent zamindar of Dhaka.
Throughout his life, Syed Taqi Mohammad held leadership positions in various social and cultural organisations. He was a member of the Hussaini Dalan Management Committee and the National Waqf Committee.
He also served as mutawalli of the Mohammadi Beg Imambara Waqf Estate, established in Old Dhaka during the Mughal era, until his death.
The kulkhani (post-funeral prayer) for the deceased will be held on Monday. The first session will take place at Hussaini Dalan after Maghrib prayers, followed by a second session at Sat Rawza Khaja Nehal Mosque after Isha prayers.
Tarun Sarkar said Syed Taqi Mohammad had assisted the Committee for Commissioning Books on Architecture by providing important information and documents for its survey of the city’s inscriptions and architectural heritage.

item.title: French senators eye stronger political engagement with Bangladesh
item.description:
A delegation of three French senators on Sunday met State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam at her office and discussed issues and ways to further strengthen political engagement between Bangladesh and France.
Senators Guillaume Chevrollier, Pierre-Alain Roiron and Olivier Henno arrived in Dhaka on Saturday night on a three-day official visit.
Ambassador of France to Bangladesh Jean-Marc Séré-Charlet and Head of the Political Wing of the Embassy Christian Bec accompanied the senators during their meeting with the State Minister.
They are part of the French-Southeast Asia and Bangladesh Senate Friendship Group, and the visit is particularly meaningful as it is the first political-level visit from France since the new democratically elected government took office in Bangladesh, said the French Embassy in Dhaka.
They will discuss strengthening political and parliamentary ties, exchange perspectives with their Bangladeshi counterparts and explore new areas of cooperation between the two countries.
The French Senate (Sénat) is the upper chamber of the French Parliament, alongside the National Assembly.
The senators are scheduled to meet the Speaker of Parliament Hafiz Uddin Ahmad and hold discussions with various Bangladeshi interlocutors.
Their program also includes visits to places associated with French development cooperation, museums, and meetings with members of the French community in Dhaka, as well as engagements with representatives of the business community.

item.title: Man’s dismembered body found in six pieces in three sacks
item.description:
Police have recovered the dismembered body of an unidentified man, cut into six pieces and packed into three plastic sacks, from beside a paddy field in Madhukhali, Faridpur.
The remains were recovered around 10am Saturday from an area near Boalia Stand in Boalia union of the upazila.
According to police and local sources, passersby spotted three tied plastic sacks at the base of a palm tree beside paddy fields belonging to Lavlu Mallick and Ishaq Miah. The sacks were found on the right side of the Faridpur-bound road, about 200 yards past Boalia Stand.
Suspecting something was wrong, locals called the national emergency service number 999. An assistant superintendent of police for the Madhukhali-Boalmari-Alphadanga circle and Sub-Inspector Masudur Rahman of Madhukhali police station later arrived at the scene with a team.
The sacks were opened in the presence of locals, revealing six severed body parts believed to be those of a man aged around 40.
Police prepared an inquest report at the scene, but the man’s identity could not immediately be established.
Masuduzzaman, ASP of the Madhukhali-Boalmari-Alphadanga circle, said the remains had been sent to Faridpur Medical College Hospital for an autopsy.
“If the identity remains unknown after the autopsy, necessary arrangements will be made to hand the body over to Anjuman Mufidul Islam for burial in accordance with religious rites,” he said.
He added that police were working to identify the deceased and determine the circumstances behind the incident.
Further legal proceedings are underway.

Complaint filed with tribunal seeking justice for Sagar-Runi murder
item.description:
A formal complaint has been filed with the Office of the Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal seeking justice for the murders of journalist couple Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi.
Runi’s brother, Naosher Roman, submitted the complaint to Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam on Sunday.
According to the complaint, Sagar Sarowar, news editor of Maasranga Television, and Meherun Runi, a senior correspondent at ATN Bangla, were murdered in their rented apartment in the capital’s West Rajabazar area between 2am and 7am on February 11, 2012.
Despite the passage of 14 years, multiple investigative agencies have failed to identify the perpetrators or make significant progress in the case, the complaint said.
It said local police, the Detective Branch (DB) and the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) had failed to make progress after the murders. The High Court subsequently directed the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) to take over the case.
However, even after the PBI investigation, the case remains unresolved, according to the complaint.
The family has therefore sought a fair and proper investigation through the International Crimes Tribunal to identify the perpetrators and bring them to justice.
The complaint also sought exemplary punishment for those responsible and requested that it be formally registered so that legal proceedings can be initiated.

item.title: Zubaida: Govt takes initiatives to ensure healthcare for marginalised communities
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s wife and Ziaur Rahman Foundation Vice Chairman Dr Zubaida Rahman has said the government has taken various initiatives to ensure healthcare reaches people in the most marginalised communities.
She made the remarks at a seminar titled “Innovation in Healthcare for All” at the Innovation Fair at Novo Theatre in Bijoy Sarani, Dhaka, on Sunday morning.
“Healthcare is not charity; it is a fundamental right,” Dr Zubaida said.
She pointed to a communication gap between researchers and healthcare providers, saying closer collaboration between the two could improve the quality of healthcare.
She also stressed the need to expand awareness programmes on cancer and diabetes.
Dr Zubaida said Bangladesh could ensure world-class healthcare by strengthening coordination between technology and researchers.
She said the government plans to restructure the health sector so that it can contribute 5% to the country’s GDP in the future.
Speaking at the event, State Minister for Health Dr MA Muhit said innovations in dengue prevention should be tested and implemented in Bangladesh.
He called for initiatives to bring Bangladeshi scientists working abroad back home and utilise their expertise.
The state minister also stressed the need to introduce a digital platform for appointment booking at all government hospitals.

Rybakina beats Sabalenka to win US Open title, takes No. 1 ranking
item.description:
Elena Rybakina defeated defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 on Saturday to win her first US Open title and complete her rise to the top of the women’s world rankings.
Rybakina had already secured the No. 1 ranking by reaching the semifinals, but capped her campaign by claiming the trophy Sabalenka had won in the previous two years.
“It’s still so difficult to process what happened,” Rybakina said. “Too many achievements these few weeks.”
The victory gave the 27-year-old her third Grand Slam title and second of the year. She also defeated Sabalenka in the Australian Open final earlier this season.
Rybakina ended Sabalenka’s 19-match winning streak at the US Open. Sabalenka had not lost at Flushing Meadows since the 2023 final against Coco Gauff.
Rybakina earned $5.5 million, the biggest prize in Grand Slam history, and joined Sabalenka and French Open champion Mirra Andreeva as the only players with three tour titles this season.
Sabalenka, who received $2.8 million, was seeking to become the first woman since Serena Williams from 2012-14 to win three consecutive US Open titles. She smashed her racket after briefly embracing Rybakina at the net.
“I was just out there competing, trying to do my best with what I had there today,” Sabalenka said. “Not good enough.”
Although Rybakina struggled with her first serve, she consistently pressured Sabalenka with her returns. She earned 12 break points and converted three, enough to secure the victory.
Rybakina’s win was the first time the lower-ranked player prevailed in a US Open women’s final between the No. 1 and No. 2 seeds since 2000.
Sabalenka had occupied the top ranking for 99 consecutive weeks, but Rybakina will take over on Monday.
Born in Russia, Rybakina represents Kazakhstan. She won her first Grand Slam at Wimbledon in 2022 and now needs only the French Open title to complete a career Grand Slam.
Sabalenka acknowledged Rybakina’s powerful serve and ability to dictate play, particularly on the fast US Open courts.
Rybakina had struggled at the US Open in previous years, never advancing beyond the fourth round before this tournament. She also briefly stopped playing during a quarterfinal match against Iga Swiatek in Cincinnati because of a foot injury but recovered in time for New York.
“I honestly was coming here for the last 10 years, and it was never successful — nothing close to that,” Rybakina said. “It’s just incredible. I’m falling in love with New York more and more.”
Sabalenka had reached the US Open final four straight times and the semifinals six times, but her impressive run at Flushing Meadows ended with Saturday’s defeat.
The Belarusian had won both of her previous meetings with Rybakina this season, at Indian Wells and Miami, and leads their career rivalry 10-8.
Rybakina took the opening set after Sabalenka struggled with her serve and became increasingly frustrated. Sabalenka recovered in the second set, breaking Rybakina late to level the match, but Rybakina quickly regained control in the decider and completed the biggest victory of her career.

item.title: Zahid: Harmonious environment essential for development
item.description:
Women and Children Affairs and Social Welfare Minister Dr AZM Zahid Hossain on Saturday stressed the need for maintaining unity and harmony among the people for development, saying that development in any area is possible only through unity, not conflicts.
“A sound and peaceful environment serves as a key prerequisite for development. If there are divisions, clashes and conflicts among the people, development activities are obstructed. But a cordial and harmonious environment facilitates development,” he said while speaking at a workers’ conference and views-exchange meeting organized by Joypur Union unit of Nawabganj upazila BNP in Dinajpur.
Addressing the local leaders and activists of the BNP, Zahid said, “If you maintain a good environment in your area, it will be easier to carry out development activities at all levels. But if conflicts arise among you, development activities will be obstructed.”
The minister stressed the need to educate children properly and develop them as competent citizens. “We have to work together to build the future generation on the foundation of humanity and moral values. Alongside ensuring a favorable environment for education, social awareness must be increased to guide the younger generation in the right direction,” he said.
“If we fail to do something good for the future generation, we will not be able to protect them from the devastating situation caused by drugs,” he added. Calling for a united social resistance against drug abuse, the minister said people involved in drug trafficking must be resisted collectively and their unethical activities stopped.
“Simply sitting at home and waiting for law enforcement agencies will not be enough to eliminate the presence of drugs in society,” he said. The minister also said it is the responsibility of society to stand beside any individual or family facing an economic crisis.

item.title: Dengue cases surge in Chittagong despite control measures
item.description:
Dengue cases have continued to rise in Chittagong, with 760 infections recorded in the first 12 days of September.
According to the Civil Surgeon’s Office, 2,795 dengue cases have been reported in Chittagong from January to September 12. Of them, 1,214 patients are from Chittagong city, 1,234 from different upazilas and 349 from other districts under the division.
Ten people have died of the mosquito-borne disease, while 262 patients are currently receiving treatment in different hospitals. Chittagong Medical College Hospital has the highest number of dengue patients.
Monthly figures show a sharp increase during the monsoon. The district recorded 68 cases in January, 22 in February, 20 in March, 29 in April, 37 in May, 122 in June, 534 in July, 1,206 in August and 760 in the first 11 days of September.
Among the 15 upazilas, Sitakunda recorded the highest number of cases at 355, followed by Karnaphuli with 195, Banshkhali 95, Rangunia 83, Raozan 67, Patiya 62, Boalkhali 49, Hathazari 37 and Mirsarai 36.
The Chittagong City Corporation (CCC) has launched a special mosquito-control campaign as dengue cases rise. A survey by its health department identified 155 potential Aedes breeding grounds across the city, including educational institutions, construction sites, abandoned buildings and residential areas.
CCC officials said eight wards have been identified as dengue hotspots. Insecticides are being sprayed at the homes of dengue patients and within a 500-metre radius.
Malaria and Mosquito Control Officer Md Sarful Islam Mahi said breeding sites have been destroyed and insecticides applied in the identified hotspots.
Civil Surgeon Dr Mohammad Sajedur Rahman said dengue prevention requires both mosquito control and the destruction of Aedes breeding grounds. He said the health department has asked the city corporation to intensify mosquito-control activities.
CCC Executive Officer and Secretary Ashraful Amin said the corporation is using BTI to destroy mosquito larvae, alongside fogging to kill adult mosquitoes. More than 100 workers have received special training for the campaign.

item.title: Rajshahi takes dengue fight to the grassroots
item.description:
Rajshahi Divisional Commissioner Yusuf Ali on Saturday called for turning dengue prevention and cleanliness activities into a social movement by encouraging people to keep their own surroundings clean.
“We must not remain dependent only on cleaners for maintaining cleanliness; rather, we need to develop the habit of cleaning our own spaces ourselves,” he said.
He made the remarks while attending a live telecast of the nationwide dengue prevention and cleanliness campaign inaugurated by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the South Plaza of the National Parliament Building.
The programme was screened through a video conference at the conference room of the Rajshahi Deputy Commissioner’s Office.
The divisional commissioner said extensive initiatives have been taken in Rajshahi as part of the three-month nationwide dengue prevention and cleanliness campaign announced by the prime minister.
In the first phase, cleanliness drives are being conducted at government offices. Educational institutions, religious institutions, dengue hotspots and drains in municipalities and city corporations across the division will gradually be brought under the campaign, he said.
Yusuf Ali said necessary instructions have been issued to Upazila Nirbahi Officers (UNOs) to implement the campaign at the grassroots level.
Initiatives have also been taken to remove stagnant water from rooftops, flower tubs and other potential mosquito-breeding sites around homes and offices, while ensuring proper cleanliness of the premises.
Volunteer organisations, including Girls Guide, Scouts and BD Clean, have been engaged to turn the campaign into a mass initiative.
The virtual conference was attended by Deputy Commissioner Kazi Shahidul Islam and Superintendent of Police Mamun Or Rashid, along with government and non-government officials and employees, teachers and students, scouts and journalists.
Following the programme, the divisional commissioner formally inaugurated the dengue prevention and cleanliness campaign in Rajshahi by participating in a cleaning drive at the premises of the Divisional Commissioner’s and Deputy Commissioner’s offices.
Earlier, a colourful rally was brought out from the Deputy Commissioner’s Office premises. The rally paraded through important roads in the city before returning to the same venue.

item.title: Hi-tech parks: PPRC discussion examines gap between mission and reality
item.description:
The Power and Participation Research Centre (PPRC) on Saturday held an episode of its Ajker Agenda virtual series titled “Hi-Tech Parks: What is the Mission? What is the Reality?”, bringing together industry leaders, former officials and policy experts to assess the performance of Bangladesh’s High-Tech and Software Technology Parks.
The discussion focused on why, despite the establishment of dozens of parks and rising budget allocations, the sector has yet to deliver results comparable to similar initiatives in other countries, and what is needed to bridge the gap between the parks’ original mission and their performance on the ground.
Dr M Rokonuzzaman, professor of the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at North South University, said Bangladesh established 39 High-Tech and Software Technology Parks between 2009 and 2023 on the assumption that infrastructure alone would drive investment and create a hi-tech boom.
“Bangladesh built 39 High-Tech and Software Technology Parks between 2009 and 2023 on the assumption that infrastructure alone would trigger a hi-tech boom and investment without effective focus on a supportive ecosystem, availability of skilled labour, and industry-academia linkage. Results so far clearly show that the assumption was not the right one, as the examples of Taiwan, South Korea, Malaysia and Singapore attest,” he said.
Mohammad Mohidul Islam, managing director of Ongsho, gave a critical assessment of the Jessore High-Tech Park, established in December 2017.
“The 40 companies currently housed in the park struggle independently for survival without effective ecosystem support. The authority treats them as tenants rather than as entrepreneurs. Trained manpower quickly leaves. Maintenance of the facility is very poor, and the costs of utilities are high,” he said.
Engr Md Ashafuddoza Shishir, co-founder and chief operating officer of Netro Systems Ltd and Telzen at Hi-Tech Park Rajshahi, offered a more positive assessment of the Rajshahi experience. He pointed to the growth of technology ventures that emerged from a 2016 incubation centre and have since developed international operations.
He, however, said: “The tangible benefit for companies in the Rajshahi Hi-Tech Park remains confined to tax exemptions, as direct authority support for startups is largely absent.”
Farhana A Rahman, chairperson and CEO of UY Systems Ltd, drawing on her experience with BASIS, said the country remained caught in a cycle of ambitious promises without sufficient progress on the ground.
“We remain trapped in a loop of grandiose promises about high-tech parks, yet despite the building of so many parks across the country, real progress on the ground remains absent. The Kaliakor Hi-Tech Park offered land plots but no supportive services, so that many later surrendered their plot allocations,” she said.
Rafel Kabir, managing director of DNS Software Ltd, attributed many of the sector’s shortcomings to government policy and sensationalist media coverage. He contrasted the light-touch regulatory environment that allowed services such as Uber and Foodpanda to expand with the top-down approach taken in developing the parks.
“Rather than relying solely on export tax incentives, High-Tech Parks should have targeted foundational technology manufacturing, like motherboard and chip fabrication, while delivering complete, EPZ-grade infrastructure,” he said.
Faiz Ahmad Taiyeb, former special assistant to the Chief Adviser of Bangladesh at the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology, reflected on his experience overseeing the sector and identified the location of the parks as a major factor behind their limited impact.
“The core failure of Bangladesh’s High-Tech Parks stems from placing heavy physical infrastructure in regions lacking a viable local economy,” he said, adding that the challenges extend beyond physical infrastructure to the credibility and effectiveness of the training ecosystem.
Summing up the discussion, moderator Hossain Zillur Rahman, executive chairman of PPRC, said: “Long-term success requires shifting focus from building physical real estate to cultivating soft infrastructure, skilled human capital, and industry-driven training.”
The discussion concluded that Bangladesh does not necessarily need to abandon the High-Tech Park model but must strengthen the foundations on which the parks operate, including reliable utilities, accountable governance and effective support systems that treat companies as partners rather than tenants.

PM to distribute 7,000 farmer cards in Feni on Thursday
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will distribute 7000 farmers' cards in Feni on September 17, as the government has set a target to distribute 16.5 million cards among farmers over the next four years, with an estimated initial cost of Taka 681 crore.
Fisheries, Livestock and Agriculture minister Mohammad Amin Ur Rashid said this after visiting Fulgazi government Pilot High School playground, where the prime minister will distribute the cards, on Saturday morning.
Under the target, the government will distribute the farmer cards among 1.10 lakh farmers across the country on that day.
Simultaneous launching ceremonies will be held in 50 districts on the same day. Bank accounts have already been opened for one lakh of the 16.30 lakh farmers registered under the program so far, ministry officials said.
Under the cash incentive program, landless, marginal and small farmers holding the card will receive Tk2,500 directly through their bank accounts. Around one lakh farmers are expected to receive the incentive on the inauguration day.
Information on another five lakh farmers has already been verified and approved for opening bank accounts, the ministry said.
“The farmer cards will be distributed in each upazila and union, and the card will be distributed among all the farmers within the scheduled time”, the minister told the function.
The government has decided to bring farmers under the card system to make subsidies, loans, and incentives more accessible to them in the agriculture sector.
Regarding the fertilizer stock, the agriculture minister said the country has no crisis of fertilizer, as a ‘vicious circle’ is trying to create anarchy in the fertilizer distribution system.
The program will be implemented in three stages – pre-pilot, pilot and nationwide expansion. In the pre-pilot phase, farmers engaged in crop production, fisheries and livestock, including dairy farmers, will be included across 11 blocks in 11 upazilas of 10 districts.
According to the ministry, the pre-pilot phase of the Farmer's Card distribution program has already been launched on Pohela Boishakh, the first day of the Bangla New Year on April 14 this year.
In the first phase, 22,065 farmers in 11 upazilas under 10 districts received the cards. Of them, 20,671 landless, marginal, and small farmers received Tk2,500 annually in direct cash assistance.
The Agriculture Ministry aims to distribute Farmer Cards to 43 lakh farmers during the 2026-27 fiscal year, out of an estimated 2.27 crore farmers nationwide.
The remaining farmers will gradually be brought under the program, according to the ministry.
Additional Secretary of the agriculture ministry Md Yasin, Director General of the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) Md Abdur Rahim, Deputy Commissioner of Feni Mohammad Mahbubul Karim, Fulgazi Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Kawser Hamid, Fulgazi Upazila assistant commissioner (land) Soheli Nawshin Protasha, BNP national executive committee assistant secretary Belal Hossen, BNP national executive committee member Abu Taleb, and Upazila BNP convener Fakhrul Alam Swapan were also present during this time.

item.title: Dismembered body parts of woman found in Adabor
item.description:
Police recovered the severed head and hand of an unidentified woman from Adabor in the capital on Saturday.
The body parts were recovered in a sack from the Hakkar Mor area of Adabor-10, said Adabor Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Zahidul Islam.

item.title: China, Russia, Iran leaders gather in India as BRICS nations seek common ground
item.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping joined the leaders of Russia, Iran, India and other BRICS nations in New Delhi on Saturday, seeking common ground on the Middle East war as deep divisions test the 11-member bloc.
Xi told the summit that the Middle East war “does not serve the common interests of the international community,” according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.
Foreign ministers of the BRICS grouping failed to agree on a joint statement when they met in New Delhi in May, with Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates divided over the war that began with US-Israeli strikes on February 28.
However, Indian diplomatic sources said leaders were working towards a joint position on some issues as the bloc seeks to bolster its global influence and address conflict, trade turbulence and energy security.
BRICS was created in 2009 as a forum for major emerging economies seeking greater influence in institutions dominated by Western powers.
“We have to transform this pyramid of privilege into a platform of partnership,” Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi told Xi, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other leaders.
Modi, opening the two-day summit, called for a system “where every country has a voice, every member has a stake, and humanity’s development is at the centre of every effort.”
He told leaders that BRICS nations “represent 50% of the world’s population, 40% of global GDP, and more than 25% of global trade.”
The Middle East conflict was high on the agenda.
India maintains cordial relations with Iran and Israel, but is also careful to strike a delicate balance in its ties with Washington.
Iran’s Pezeshkian attended the summit shortly after warning that the Middle East does not need the United States to be a “regional policeman,” with the two countries at war and tensions threatening the vital Strait of Hormuz.
UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan is also at the summit in New Delhi, as is Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan is expected to join later on Saturday.
India has navigated the energy crisis caused by the US-Iran war in part by turning to Russia, despite Moscow’s war in Ukraine and pressure from Washington and other Western capitals.
Modi embraced Putin before talks on Friday. Putin, who last visited India in December 2025, is one of New Delhi’s most important strategic partners.
But the summit’s other major focus is China.
Xi’s visit is also being closely watched because it is his first to neighboring India since 2019, and the biggest step yet in a cautious thaw between the nuclear-armed rivals.
Xi was given a red-carpet welcome, with an honor guard of soldiers and traditional dancers in colorful dresses, and greeted with a handshake by Modi at the summit venue.
His visit comes six years after a deadly military clash along their disputed Tibetan border, with ties gradually improving through restored flights, visas and high-level contacts.
Beijing said ahead of his visit that it was “ready to work with India... by strengthening communication, enhancing cooperation, and properly handling differences.”
The underlying territorial dispute remains unresolved, and both sides retain heavy military deployments along their roughly 3,500-kilometre (2,175-mile) high-altitude border with Tibet.
Xi is due to hold face-to-face talks with Modi later on Saturday, according to New Delhi’s foreign ministry.
“They are looking for ‘early and substantial harvest’ when it comes to the border issue,” said Pradeep Taneja, a China-India expert at the University of Melbourne.
“You cannot have a build-up of your forces on the border... but at the same time say ‘we should continue to have people-to-people relations and economic relationships.’”
Deep mistrust remains, with their contested Himalayan frontier, a widening trade deficit and strategic rivalry continuing to complicate ties.
Dozens of Tibetans protested in New Delhi on Friday -- exiles, like their Buddhist leader the Dalai Lama, who has lived in India since fleeing a Chinese crackdown in 1959 -- waving placards against Xi’s visit.

item.title: Zelensky says willing to meet Putin at G20 in Miami
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he would be willing to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin at a G20 summit in December, in an interview released Saturday, as efforts intensify to end the conflict.
Washington is seeking to kick-start long-stalled negotiations to find a solution to the conflict, Europe’s deadliest since World War II, with US negotiators recently visiting Kyiv and Moscow and President Donald Trump and Putin this week holding talks on the conflict over the phone.
The United States holds this year’s presidency of the Group of 20 major economies, which comprises 19 countries plus the European Union and the African Union, and culminates in a leaders’ summit in Miami in December.
Russia’s finance minister has already attended one G20 meeting, causing discomfort among some of Ukraine’s allies, and a Russian diplomat said Saturday that Moscow will also send some officials to a G20 energy meeting in Houston next week.
Asked whether he would be willing to meet Putin at the December summit if both leaders were invited, Zelensky told German broadcaster Deutsche Welle: “Yes, of course.”
“We have to come. We have to meet, to speak, and make decisions.
“It’s not about words. What I will tell him or what he wants to tell me, it doesn’t matter. It doesn’t matter. Matters only result. Result matters. That’s it.”
Last weekend, US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Moscow and Putin and Trump also discussed the war earlier in the week in what the Kremlin termed an “extremely frank” and constructive hour-long phone call.
In the Deutsche Welle interview, which took place Friday in Canada, Zelensky said that Witkoff and Kushner’s visit was a “good signal,” and it was important the pair had visited Kyiv as well as Moscow.
“It’s respect to our people,” he said.
Zelensky has also announced he plans to meet Trump in late September, as Washington pushes for fresh face-to-face talks between Moscow and Kyiv.
Asked about Ukraine’s position ahead of possible negotiations, Zelensky responded: “Ukraine now is much stronger than last year on the battlefield.”
Russia was sustaining heavy battlefield losses, paying a “big price” for “very slow moves on the battlefield.” he said.
“That’s why we think that we have a good position for negotiations.”
Kyiv has said the talks could happen as early as this month, but the Kremlin on Monday said it was “too early” to discuss a venue or dates.
Several previous rounds of negotiations have failed. Trust between the sides is low, and there is no sign that Moscow or Kyiv have shifted their positions.
Both Moscow and Kyiv have escalated long-range strikes on each other in recent months, leading to the highest civilian death toll since the early days of the war.
Zelensky also repeated his call for Ukraine’s allies to provide more interceptor missiles to fend off Russian air attacks.
“Russia produces... today 140 ballistic missiles per month. So, according to the rules of Nato, if you want to destroy 140, you need 280... You will never have 280 missiles per month,” he said.
It was a “huge challenge” to have 100 a month, he said.

item.title: Chhatra Dal leader missing after falling into Padma River
item.description:
A local leader of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) went missing after falling into the Padma River when a boat carrying 123 people hit a pillar of the Hardinge Bridge in Bheramara upazila of Kushtia district on Friday night.
The Chhatra Dal leader was identified as Rakibuzzaman Rocky, member secretary of the Shailkupa municipality unit JCD in Jhenaidah.
Mohammad Zahedur Rahman, Officer-in-Charge of Bheramara Police Station, said a group of people hired a boat to visit the Solaiman Shah Shrine in Bheramara from Katla Ghat in Shailkupa of Jhenaidah district.
When the boat was returning after visiting the shrine, it was hit by a strong current, causing it to collide with a pillar of the bridge.
At one point, three people, including Rocky, fell into the river as the rear portion of the bulkhead boat collided with pillar No. 4 of the Hardinge Bridge.
Two of the victims, Liton and Wahab, were rescued, but Rocky remained missing.
Divers from the local fire service conducted a rescue operation but failed to trace Rocky until 1am on Saturday.
Bheramara Upazila Nirbahi Officer Mohammad Amirul Arafat, who visited the scene, said darkness and the strong river current were making the rescue operation difficult, while several government units were working at the scene.
Assistant Director of Kushtia Fire Service and Civil Defence Wadud Hossain said: “Due to the strong current in the Padma, it has become difficult to conduct the search operation at night.”
